clue.text: A friend's taken aback? Oddly not he, by joint reprimand

indicators.note: something taken aback is pushed backwards, so the word for friends is read from its end
done oddly means done in a strange way, so the two little words are rearranged
by means next to, so the final piece is set alongside what came before

blocks.note: taken as written
pals are friends; the 's stands for 'is'
the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
the wrist is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked when a friend gets an odd telling-off over a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: A + PALS backwards (SLAP) + NOT HE rearranged (ON THE) + WRIST gives A SLAP ON THE WRIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap on the wrist is an idiom for a mild punishment or telling-off, which is what a reprimand is.

clue.text: In reality, a staff car to me is misused carrying a leader from there

indicators.note: letters that are misused are put to the wrong work, so they are jumbled into a new order
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be jumbled
taken as written, carried along with the rest
the first letter of there, also carried along

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a staff car is being misused, ferrying a boss from some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' adds the extra A and T into the jumble: A STAFF CAR TO ME plus A plus T rearranges to AS A MATTER OF FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial ways of saying 'actually' or 'truly', used to correct or emphasise.

clue.text: Nothing raised about winning garden plant

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is read upwards, from bottom to top
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score
a team that is up is ahead, i.e. winning

explanation.surface: A gardener reports a plant flourishing from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means the word for nothing is written bottom to top before it wraps round the word for winning.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a familiar flowering plant with tall spikes of blooms, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Small-minded over child pocketing a shilling from money kept for small expenses

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece is enclosed by another
in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: petty means small-minded or mean-spirited
ch is the dictionary abbreviation for child
taken as written
s was the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited person is grudging a child a shilling from the office kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was an old British coin worth one twentieth of a pound; its abbreviation s comes from the Latin solidus.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty cash is the small fund an office keeps on hand for minor purchases.

clue.text: Posy could make beak happy

blocks.note: beak is slang for a nose
gay in its older sense means cheerful or happy

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers might cheer up a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers, the same thing as a posy.

clue.text: Crashed — injured — was in front

blocks.note: hurt means injured
someone who led was in front

explanation.surface: A race report: a driver crashed and was hurt while leading.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash along can mean to rush noisily and violently, which is what hurtled describes.

clue.text: Spotted over there getting rid of her rubbish

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word for seen is read backwards
getting rid of means throwing out, so some letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: saw means spotted
taken as written, before trimming
these letters are the ones thrown out

explanation.surface: Someone saw a woman over there dumping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: SAW backwards is WAS; THERE without HER is TE; together WASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is unwanted material thrown away, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Just the same dialect in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be scattered

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast uses the very same regional accent as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, with no difference at all.

clue.text: Mistakenly thought to be Bristol-born actor editor valued too lightly

blocks.note: to be taken for someone is to be mistaken for them
the film star Cary Grant was born in Bristol, England
ed is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is mistaken for a famous Bristol-born film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Cary Grant, the Hollywood leading man, was born Archibald Leach in Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken for granted is not properly appreciated, so its worth is underrated.

clue.text: Inordinate praise given about favourite bonne bouche?

indicators.note: inordinate means unrestrained or out of order, so the letters are disordered
given about means placed around, so one word goes around another

blocks.note: the letters to be disordered
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A favourite little titbit is showered with lavish praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inordinate' sits beside 'praise' as if describing flattery, but it tells you to rearrange those letters around the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonne bouche is French for a tasty morsel, especially one served before a meal; the question mark flags the loose fit to appetiser.

clue.text: Smooth head of salad vegetable

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of salad
a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A smooth lettuce head in a salad of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes a glossy, smooth surface, as of hair or fur.

clue.text: Displease girl round end of day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is round in shape
last letter of day

explanation.surface: A girl is upset to be sent round at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate or displease them.

clue.text: Girl has undershirt on in Texas resort

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a vest is an undershirt in British English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl wears her undershirt at a Texas beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is the sleeveless undergarment Americans call an undershirt or tank top.
explanation.definitionFit: Galveston is a city on a Gulf Coast island in Texas, known for its beaches.

clue.text: Suitable for children to have a look at in outskirts of tiny Italian region

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last
in means placed inside, so these pieces sit within others

blocks.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, fit for children
to scan is to have a look at something
first and last letters of tiny

explanation.surface: A children's guide to looking around the edges of a small Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: U + SCAN goes inside T...Y. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy, home to Florence and Siena.

clue.text: Awareness shown by one in judgement

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter is put within the larger word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sentence is a court's judgement

explanation.surface: A judge shows awareness in passing judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, a form of consciousness.

clue.text: Actually, daughter has to face criminal

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent into another order

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It turns out a daughter must face a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for 'in fact', describing what really is the case rather than officially.

clue.text: Mineral could bring kids wealth

blocks.note: to kid someone is to fool them, so kids is a verb meaning fools
gold stands for wealth or riches

explanation.surface: A mineral find might make children rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' reads as children, but it is a verb: kids = FOOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fool's gold is iron pyrite, a mineral whose shine is mistaken for real gold.

clue.text: Large farms controlled game, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to run something is to control it
chess is a board game, to be cut short

explanation.surface: Big farms were run like a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranches are large farms, especially for raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Problem about article on court in sacred place

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
an is the indefinite article
ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A dispute over an article about a court hearing in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the article before the court abbreviation; both then sit inside the word for problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a holy place, from the Latin for sacred, as in the inner sanctum of a temple.

clue.text: Sold illicitly in Merseyside town close to Melling

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Bootle is a town in Merseyside, just north of Liverpool
last letter of Melling

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods traded in a Merseyside town near the village of Melling.
explanation.walkthrough: Bootle is a town by Liverpool docks; Melling is a nearby Merseyside village, which makes 'close to' read as nearness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods are made or sold illegally, such as smuggled liquor or pirated recordings.

clue.text: Bars in street brought in writers

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so the short abbreviation is placed within the other word

blocks.note: biros are ballpoint pens, named after their inventor
st is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Writers were brought into the bars on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the everyday British word for a ballpoint pen, after its inventor László Bíró.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistros are small informal restaurants or bars, often serving wine.

clue.text: Just financial institutions in an Alaskan city

blocks.note: fair means just
banks are financial institutions

explanation.surface: Only banks are found in a certain Alaskan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'only', but it means FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairbanks is the largest city in the interior of Alaska.

clue.text: Phone, but line's dead in this shady place

indicators.note: a dead line is gone, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: the blower is British slang for the telephone
L is the abbreviation for line; it is removed

explanation.surface: A caller in a shady garden spot finds the phone line has gone dead.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOWER minus L. 'The blower' is old British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shaded garden retreat under trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Female graduate identifying ancient kingdom

blocks.note: she is the female pronoun
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A woman graduate pins down the site of an ancient kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom of the biblical queen, usually placed in southern Arabia.

clue.text: Italian in East Virginia making musical

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter sits within the other pieces

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: An Italian putting on a musical in East Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for Italian is a crossword staple from the old bar order gin and It, meaning Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: A good modern US vice president

blocks.note: taken as written
g is the abbreviation for good
new means modern

explanation.surface: A decent, up-to-date American vice president.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew was vice president under Richard Nixon until he resigned in 1973.

clue.text: Bomber in Trier, sort to be taken out

indicators.note: taken out suggests being knocked apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A bomber in the German city of Trier is a sort who must be eliminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber who plants explosives for political ends is a terrorist.

clue.text: Handles imported product in place of pilgrimage

indicators.note: a product is something made, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be made into something new

explanation.surface: A trader handles imported goods in a pilgrims' shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' looks like a noun in the merchant picture, but it signals that the two words before it are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Promised Land is Canaan, the goal of the Israelites' journey, and figuratively any longed-for destination.
